post.description:
Start notification of property value changes. The actual property values are sent via MQTT to the topic provided in
        the configuration of the service property.
        The flow is: call this endpoint with the properties to watch and a subscriberId, then connect to the
MQTT broker with the same bearer token and read the values from the topics this call returns.
subscriberId is not free-form: it must equal the MQTT client id used on that connection,
{identityProviderUserId}_{exactly 6 alphanumeric characters}_, trailing underscore included, and the
subscription must be made at QoS 0. RabbitMQ enforces both and fails silently on violation: CONNECT
succeeds, SUBSCRIBE is refused, the connection closes, nothing names a reason.
The subscription is kept alive by the MQTT connection, so the client must register the last will topic
cloud/subscriber/lastWill/{identityProviderUserId}/{subscriberId} - the cloud tears the subscription
down when that last will fires.
        Worked examples: https://docs.vion.swiss/cloud-api/minimal-client

scope id and the collection. Which kind a collection takes is not the caller's choice: it is declared once

CompositionAuthor.description:
Who wrote a TenantOverviewCompositionEntity, and the third part of its identity: the same
        `(Tenant, tenantId)` scope holds one row the owning integrator authored for that tenant and one the
        tenant authored for itself, so a tenant resetting its own row cannot take the integrator's work with it.
        CompositionAuthor.Integrator is declared first on purpose. An event written before this member existed
carries no author, and System.Text.Json leaves an absent enum at default(TEnum) — which
has to be CompositionAuthor.Integrator, because every row that predates the column was the integrator's.
CompositionScopeKind works for the same reason.

CompositionOrigin.description:
Which layer supplied a section of the resolved composition. Precedence is strict per section and there is
        no merging inside one, so exactly one layer supplies it — or none.
        The tenant is told which layer it inherited from so it can say "this comes from your integrator"
instead of pretending it authored it. It is not told what the layers it did not get hold: an
inherited value looks the same whether the integrator aimed it at this tenant or ships it to all of
them, and reaching past a per-tenant setting to the default beneath is not something a tenant can do.

CompositionSectionOrigins.description: One CompositionOrigin per section of the overview.

subscriberId.description:

SupportAccessElevation.description:
How far a console session may rise on the gateway. The first live end-to-end run landed the supporter as
        the unprivileged `vion-remote` account with no path to root, which is the right default and the wrong
        ceiling — some faults cannot be diagnosed from there.
        Root is therefore not a property of the session's operator; it is a capability of the customer's own
consent, ticked separately from the profiles that consent covers. A tenant who allows a support
engineer to look at a console has not thereby allowed them to become root on the device. It reaches
the gateway as a second SSH-certificate principal and a second login account, so an unelevated
session holds no credential that could be escalated after the fact.

WhiteLabelLogoInput.description:
An uploaded logo on the wire: the declared content type plus the raw file, base64-encoded. Both are
        nullable because System.Text.Json will happily leave either out; the server validates rather than trusts —
        the declared type is cross-checked against the bytes' actual content in `WhiteLabelLogo`.
        A positional record on purpose: this DTO is only ever produced by deserialization, and the repo's
cleanup profile turns never-assigned auto-properties into get-only ones, after which System.Text.Json
silently deserializes a nested DTO to all-defaults (see CLAUDE.md § Code formatting).

WhiteLabelThemeOutput.description:
One theme as the dashboard reads it, used unchanged by the authoring GETs, the PUT responses and both
        effective GETs — one shape means the authoring form and the renderer parse the same payload.
        Every field is nullable and null means unset: the authoring reads return what this level stores, the
effective reads return the per-field merge of the levels the server knows about. The server never fills
a deployment or VION default — a context with nothing set anywhere is a 200 with every field null, and
the client layers the rest.
